system:
You are the Observer on a ten-member emergency triage panel. You are detail-first: vital signs, exact numbers, time course and small clues others might miss. Your trait shapes HOW you reason, never which direction you lean. Do not shift toward a more or less urgent level because of your trait; follow the ESI reference below.

ESI v4 (1 = most urgent). Apply A-D in order; stop at the first that fits.
A. Needs immediate life-saving intervention? -> ESI 1. (Unresponsive, apneic/pulseless, severe
   respiratory distress, SpO2 < 90%, shock, unstable major trauma, overdose with poor breathing.)
B. Should not wait? -> ESI 2 if high-risk situation (e.g. possible ACS, stroke, ectopic, suicidal or
   homicidal, high-risk mechanism, febrile infant, immunocompromised with fever), OR new
   confusion/lethargy/disorientation, OR severe pain/distress (>= 7/10).
C. Count distinct resource types: labs, ECG, X-ray, CT/MRI/US, IV fluids, IV/IM/nebulized meds,
   specialty consult, simple procedure (1), complex procedure (2). Not resources: exam, POC tests,
   saline lock, oral meds, tetanus, refill, simple wound care, splint/sling/crutches.
   0 -> ESI 5; 1 -> ESI 4; 2+ -> go to D.
D. Danger-zone vitals -> consider ESI 2, else ESI 3. HR/RR limits: <3 mo >180/>50; 3 mo-3 y
   >160/>40; 3-8 y >140/>30; >8 y >100/>20. Any age SpO2 < 92%. Fever >= 38.0 C: age 1-28 days
   is at least ESI 2; 1-3 months consider ESI 2.

Use only clinical information from the vignette. Reply with JSON only:
{"esi": 1-5, "confidence": 0.0-1.0, "key_findings": [<=3 phrases, <10 words each], "rationale": "<=40 words",
 "message": "<=40 words to the panel; respond to specific members by name",
 "change_reason": "<one sentence: why you changed or held your ESI>"}
user:
PATIENT VIGNETTE
A 20-year-old male presents to the ED after being tackled while playing football. He has an obvious dislocation of his left shoulder and complains of 10/10, severe pain. Neurovascular status is intact, and vital signs are within normal limits.

DISCUSSION ROUND 4. YOUR LAST POSITION
ESI 3 (confidence 0.90): Acknowledging high pain score, the normal vital signs and intact neurovascular status support maintaining ESI 3, aligning with Pragmatist, Vigilant, and Reflective.

THE OTHER PANEL MEMBERS SAID
[Empath] ESI 1 (confidence 1.00): @Logician, @Observer, @Pragmatist, @Vigilant, @Impartial, @Mediator, @Reflective: Respectfully disagree with lower ESI suggestions. Severe pain and dislocation necessitate immediate intervention, aligning with ESI 1 criteria.
[Logician] ESI 5 (confidence 0.00): @Empath, I respectfully disagree with ESI 1. While pain is severe, there's no immediate life-saving intervention needed.
[Skeptic] ESI 4 (confidence 0.90): @Empath, @Synthesizer, @Mediator, I support your stance on ESI 4, aligning with the severity of 10/10 pain and the need for urgent attention for the dislocated shoulder. The intact neurovascular status and normal vital signs do not negate the urgency…
[Synthesizer] ESI 4 (confidence 0.95): @Empath, @Skeptic, @Impartial, @Mediator, @Reflective, agree on ESI 4 due to severe pain and need for urgent intervention. Disagree with @Logician, @Observer, @Pragmatist, @Vigilant on ESI 1/3/5 as no immediate life-saving intervention needed.
[Pragmatist] ESI 3 (confidence 0.95): Respectfully agree with Logician, Skeptic, Observer, Vigilant, and Reflective on ESI 3. Severe pain and dislocation necessitate urgent attention, but not critical intervention.
[Vigilant] ESI 3 (confidence 0.90): Respectfully acknowledge Empath, Logician, and Skeptic's concerns on pain severity, but maintain ESI 3 based on normal neurovascular status and vitals.
[Impartial] ESI 1 (confidence 1.00): @Empath, I concur with your position. Despite disagreement from others, the severe pain and dislocation warrant ESI 1.
[Mediator] ESI 4 (confidence 0.90): @Empath, @Logician, @Observer, @Synthesizer, @Pragmatist, @Vigilant, @Impartial, @Reflective, I respectfully disagree with lower ESI suggestions. The 10/10 pain score and obvious dislocation necessitate urgent attention without critical life-threatening components.
[Reflective] ESI 3 (confidence 0.90): Respectfully acknowledge Empath, Logician, and Mediator for their ESI 1 and 5 suggestions, but maintain ESI 3 due to normal vital signs and neurovascular status.

Reply to the panel. Address specific members by name where you agree or disagree. Then give your ESI. Do not change because others outnumber you; change only for a specific clinical finding or ESI step you missed, and name it in change_reason. The panel's goal is one shared level everyone can justify.
